name: Ice skate
blurb: Different from roller skating: a thin blade on a slippery edge. The trick is learning to use the edges rather than trying to stay flat.
gear: Hire skates that are laced properly and tightly at the ankle
Gloves — always, because of other people’s blades
A helmet is sensible while learning
steps: Lace properly: loose at the toes, very tight over the ankle, snug at the top. Floppy ankles make skating impossible.
Learn to fall and get up on the ice, away from the barrier, before anything else.
March on the spot on the ice to get used to the blades, then march forward.
Learn to glide on two feet, then one, with knees bent and weight slightly forward.
Learn the snowplough stop, then progress to a proper one-foot stop.
Learn to push out to the side with the whole blade edge — this is the difference between marching and skating.
tips: Skate away from the barrier as soon as possible. Holding on teaches your body the wrong balance entirely.
Keep your gloves on. Fingers under blades is the classic rink injury.
proof: You skate a full lap with proper glides, stop under control, and get up unaided after a fall.
